scenario: Legacy payment EOD restart/resume after durable internal or external financial effects.

root_cause_clusters.RC-IDENTITY: Replay identity and cycle provenance are conflated.
root_cause_clusters.RC-ELIGIBILITY: Debit capacity and account eligibility omit financial obligations or state.
root_cause_clusters.RC-RESUME: Durable posting/reservation state is treated as a request to execute again.
root_cause_clusters.RC-ACCOUNTING: Ledger/reconciliation controls validate aggregates too weakly or with wrong scope.
root_cause_clusters.RC-CLOSE: Publication and completion are advanced before their control prerequisites.
root_cause_clusters.RC-DB: Database boundaries do not enforce exactly-once financial state.

defects.observable_failure: Commercially similar prior history can be reported as an accepted source replay.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Fixing PAYDUP alone is insufficient because the shell can still set source_seen from commercial similarity.

defects.observable_failure: History written by the current cycle can be treated as prior replay evidence on a rerun.
defects.partial_fix_trap: A source-only query still misclassifies restart work unless cycle provenance is excluded.

defects.observable_failure: PAYDUP classifies commercial similarity as DUPLICATE.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Correct history flags still fail if the COBOL decision merges similarity with identity.

defects.observable_failure: Blocked internal beneficiaries are treated as eligible.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Shell-side checks cannot protect direct COBOL callers or later routing decisions.

defects.observable_failure: Total debit can omit fee and tax.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Capacity and ledger logic may each still compute a different obligation after one formula is fixed.

defects.observable_failure: Capacity can ignore other active reservations for the payer.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Using the full debit still overstates available capacity when outstanding reservations are excluded.

defects.observable_failure: Shell capacity derives available funds from an incomplete reservation population.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Correct PAYCAP arithmetic is fed the wrong reserved amount unless the database population is fixed.

defects.observable_failure: Existing internal postings can be routed as fresh work.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Shell resume detection is insufficient if the COBOL route decision still requests execution.

defects.observable_failure: Existing external reservations can be routed as a new reservation request.
defects.partial_fix_trap: A reservation lookup alone cannot prevent duplicate financial work if the route decision ignores it.

defects.observable_failure: A reservation with a mismatched amount can be accepted for resume.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Existence is not consistency; downstream clearing can otherwise publish the wrong obligation.

defects.observable_failure: An existing clearing item can be recreated instead of kept.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Reservation idempotency does not protect the clearing boundary.

defects.observable_failure: Restart inspection can accept inconsistent durable external state.
defects.partial_fix_trap: COBOL decisions receive misleading state flags unless restart inspection validates relationships.

defects.observable_failure: Restart inspection can accept an inconsistent existing internal posting.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Idempotent routing is unsafe if the stored posting does not match the selected payment.

defects.observable_failure: Internal resume can reapply account balances after a posting already exists.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Preserving the posting row is not enough if balance mutation is not guarded by the same exactly-once boundary.

defects.observable_failure: External resume can create another active reservation.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Route-level resume still duplicates money state unless insertion is protected by durable identity.

defects.observable_failure: The database permits duplicate active financial state for one payment.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Application checks alone remain race-prone and do not make the database authoritative.

defects.observable_failure: Ledger validation can accept an incomplete route-specific ledger shape.
defects.partial_fix_trap: A balanced aggregate can still omit tax, fee, principal or clearing obligations.

defects.observable_failure: Resume can leave a successful payment with missing ledger obligations.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Financial idempotency alone does not reconstruct accounting state that was only partially written.

defects.observable_failure: Reconciliation can declare success from ledger equality while other financial invariants are broken.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Correct ledger shape still cannot prove reservation, clearing, population and lifecycle consistency.

defects.observable_failure: Reconciliation metrics can include rows from another cycle.
defects.partial_fix_trap: A correct decision program still receives polluted counts when shell queries are not cycle-scoped.

defects.observable_failure: External reservation and clearing totals can be compared without all charges.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Ledger balance does not prove the reserved debit equals clearing plus fee and tax.

defects.observable_failure: Population counts can ignore rejected or held business when deciding a cycle is balanced.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Financial totals may balance even though not every selected payment has a valid terminal or durable intermediate state.

defects.observable_failure: Publication can be allowed when reconciliation is held.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Removing stale files later cannot undo publication if the decision itself is permissive.

defects.observable_failure: A held rerun can leave official artifacts created by an earlier successful attempt.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Correct publication decisions still leak stale outputs unless the filesystem is normalized before/after a held rerun.

defects.observable_failure: Close can ignore report or archive completion prerequisites.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Delivery acknowledgement alone is insufficient for authorization.

defects.observable_failure: Balanced but not closable work can remain PENDING instead of durable RECONCILED/WAITING state.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Fixing authorization gating alone leaves restart state ambiguous on the next invocation.

defects.observable_failure: Completion state can advance before all close controls are satisfied.
defects.partial_fix_trap: The authorization file can be withheld while the database is already incorrectly completed.

defects.observable_failure: Database lifecycle constraints permit authorization without a completed balanced cycle.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Shell checks are not authoritative if direct or future writes can violate the same invariant.

defects.observable_failure: A balanced internal-only cycle can fail publication because the clearing CSV has no data rows.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Close logic never runs if a legitimate zero-row clearing interface is mistaken for a publication failure.

requirements: Replay identity uses already-accepted source reference, not commercial similarity.
Eligibility and capacity account for blocked participants, full debit and active reservations.
Restart routing treats durable posting/reservation/clearing state as authority and validates consistency.
Database-backed financial effects are exactly once across reruns.
Ledger obligations and reconciliation cover complete route-specific financial state with cycle scope.
Publication is gated by balanced reconciliation and held reruns remove stale official files.
Completion/authorization requires delivery, report and archive prerequisites and remains idempotent.
